### What problem does this solve?

right now this is only really human usable from a TUI or CLI, that's a problem!

### Proposed solution

add to vibey as many human usable UIs as possible, including:
- android app
- ios app
- macos desktop app
- linux desktop app
- nextjs web app

the only thing to ignore is anything windows specific
all UI platforms need to work on the completely sovereign version
and paid LLMs can be added from there as needed by the human user

### Alternatives considered

_No response_

### Anything else?

_No response_

## Triage — 2026-09-17 (`develop` @ f2467910, v0.8.0)

**Status: NOT STARTED** · size **XL** · confidence high

**The ask, as read:** Add as many human-usable UI surfaces to vibey as possible — Android app, iOS app, macOS desktop app, Linux desktop app, and a Next.js web app — all working against the fully sovereign (local-only) configuration, with paid LLMs addable afterwards; explicitly excluding anything Windows-specific.

### What already ships
- The CLI (`vibey`, 21 commands incl. new/answer/work/watch/status/engines/cost/ledger show/deploy */doctor/operator/worker) — src/vibey/cli/main.py, wired through pyproject.toml:32
- A single-screen Textual dashboard reachable as `vibey watch`, plus a replay app — src/vibey/tui/dashboard.py:205,370, invoked from src/vibey/cli/main.py:501-565
- Desktop OS notifications (not an app) and an outbound signed webhook publisher — src/vibey/infrastructure/notify/desktop.py, src/vibey/infrastructure/notify/webhook.py

### Evidence in the tree
- pyproject.toml:31-32 — `[project.scripts]` declares exactly one entry point, `vibey = "vibey.cli.main:app"`; there is no `vibey-server`, no second UI binary
- src/vibey/cli/main.py:67 — `app = typer.Typer(name="vibey", ...)`; the 21 commands at src/vibey/cli/main.py:164,233,270,392,420,485,493,501,568,616,700,739,792,843,886,934,966,998,1030,1183,1206 are the entire human surface besides the TUI
- src/vibey/cli/main.py:501-565 — `@app.command("watch")` is the only path into the TUI; it imports `VibeyDashboardApp` and `fetch_dashboard_state` from vibey.tui.dashboard and runs it
- src/vibey/tui/dashboard.py:205 — `class VibeyDashboardApp(App[None])` is a single-screen dashboard (panels at :136 StatusPanel, :155 QueuePanel, :166 CircuitsPanel, :177 WorktreesPanel, :191 LedgerPanel) plus `VibeyReplayApp` at :370; no projects list, no gates screen, no log drill-down
- tests/tui/test_dashboard.py:22,67,151,247,295 — 5 tests total; the TUI is a skeleton, exactly as runbook 08 describes
- src/vibey/ (directory listing) — packages are application, cli, domain, infrastructure, tui only; there is no http/, api/, or server/ package anywhere under src/vibey
- …and 7 more

### What is actually left
- Build the HTTP API the clients speak to (`vibey server`, FastAPI + OpenAPI schema): projects, jobs, gates, engines, budget resources mirroring the application layer, with the API-token auth scheme. Nothing in src/vibey exposes HTTP today — this is the hard prerequisite for every non-terminal surface.
- Add the log-depth streaming endpoint (`GET /projects/{id}/logs`, SSE or WebSocket) with the `phase | job | ledger | engine | raw` depth parameter and cursor-based ledger backfill, per docs/runbooks/expansion/08-clients.md:24-35.
- Generate a typed TypeScript client package from the OpenAPI schema (`@vibey/sdk`) as the shared dependency of the web, mobile, and desktop surfaces.
- Create clients/web/ — Next.js App Router application: projects list, phase pipeline, queue with lease ages, gate answering (including the `--raw` JSON grammar from src/vibey/cli/main.py:284), engines/health/rotation, budget, and the log drill-down; SSE for live updates; Playwright e2e against a scripted-engine fixture server.
- Create clients/mobile/ — React Native/Expo app covering iOS and Android from one codebase: park/gate answering, budget approvals, and the depth-controlled log viewer.
- Add an APNs/FCM push relay publisher behind the existing publisher seam (src/vibey/infrastructure/notify/service.py) so parked jobs reach a phone.
- Create clients/desktop/ — Tauri shell wrapping the web UI, with tray showing live phase; bundle macOS dmg and Linux AppImage + deb + rpm (covers Ubuntu/Fedora/Arch); no Windows target per the issue.
- Finish the TUI to the same screen set (currently one dashboard, 5 tests) so it is a first-class surface rather than a skeleton — src/vibey/tui/dashboard.py.
- …and 3 more

### Blockers
- No HTTP API exists in the conductor at all — every surface today is the CLI/TUI talking straight to Postgres (src/vibey/tui/dashboard.py imports PostgresLedgerRepository and PostgresProjectRepository directly). Until `vibey server` exists, none of the five requested clients can be started.
- Toolchain and account prerequisites the repository does not have: Node, Rust (Tauri), an Expo account, and — only at store-submission time (workstream 07) — Apple and Google developer accounts.
- The repository currently has no TypeScript or Rust CI lane; adding one is a precondition, not an afterthought, because the existing gates are Python-only per CLAUDE.md.

**Notes:** The issue's own premise is still exactly true today: CLI and TUI are the only human surfaces. This is a genuine multi-platform greenfield build, not a gap in something half-shipped. Runbook docs/runbooks/expansion/08-clients.md describes the whole design in detail, but per the audit rules a runbook is not an implementation — the master plan itself grades it "Not started" as of 2026-09-15, and nothing in PRs #181-#207 touched it (git log since 2026-09-01 on src/vibey/tui/ and 08-clients.md shows only doc commits #156 and a URL repoint). One scoping caution: the issue asks for five platforms, but Android+iOS collapse to one React Native codebase and macOS+Linux collapse to one Tauri shell, so the real unit count is web + RN + Tauri + the API, which is still multi-week.


<sub>Automated triage pass: every open issue re-read against the tree at `develop@f2467910`, each verdict then attacked by an independent verifier whose job was to refute it. Supersedes the 2026-09-15 triage, which was measured at 0.7.0.</sub>
